nodes.text: Let $f(k)$ be the minimal $N$ such that if $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ is $k$-coloured then there is a monochromatic solution to $a+b=c$. Estimate $f(k)$. In particular, is it true that $f(k) < c^k$ for some constant $c>0$?

#483 : [Er61,p.233] [Er65,p.188] number theory | additive combinatorics | ramsey theory The values of $f(k)$ are known as Schur numbers. The best-known bounds for large $k$ are\[(380)^{k/5}-O(1)\leq f(k) \leq (e-\tfrac{1}{6}) k!.\]Note that $380^{1/5}\approx 3.2806$. The lower bound is due to Ageron, Casteras, Pellerin, Portella, Rimmel, and Tomasik [ACPPRT21] (improving previous bounds of Exoo [Ex94] and Fredricksen and Sweet [FrSw00] ). The upper bound is due to Xu, Xie, and Chen [XXC02] (improving previous bounds of Wan [Wa97] and Whitehead [Wh73] ). See Eliahou [El19] for more on the upper bound. The known values of $f$ are $f(1)=2$, $f(2)=5$, $f(3)=14$, $f(4)=45$, and $f(5)=161$ (see A030126 ). (The equality $f(5)=161$ was established by Heule [He17] ). See also [183] (in particular a folklore observation gives $f(k)\leq R(3;k)-1$).
